problem: Existing navigation world models reconstruct future pixels or features conditioned only on the factual dataset actions. This is misaligned with planning, which needs counterfactual evaluation of alternative actions, and it adds unnecessary complexity and compounding error.
motivation: Robot data is expensive and action-annotated data is scarce, so world models are attractive for evaluating actions and learning policies offline. In navigation, spatial proximity correlates with latent feature similarity, so predicting compatibility with the goal should suffice, with no reconstruction needed.
key_idea: Train a latent world model that predicts, for cross-trajectory counterfactual action sequences, a compatibility score with the goal (regressed to a log-distance label) instead of reconstructing observations, then use it as a pseudo-labeler and a GRPO reward model for policy learning.
insight: Sampling counterfactual action sequences from other trajectories is the key ingredient: M=1 gives ACC3 of 34.19 vs 70.46 at M=16 on SCAND (Table 4), and gains saturate as M grows. MSE regression to a -log distance label beats contrastive loss (ACC3 36.0 vs 90.6, Table 5), because it captures the magnitude of differences and focuses on hard negatives. Pixel-generating NWM plans worst, so visual plausibility does not imply geometric consistency.
method: Latent encoding and prediction: a ViT encoder (DINOv2-S or CroCo-v2-B) encodes observations, an MLP embeds each action into a token, and a causal Transformer decoder (6 layers) predicts K-1 future latent states autoregressively.
Compatibility discriminator: a 4-layer Transformer decoder plus a linear head scores each predicted latent against the goal image latent, giving an M_counter x (K-1) score matrix.

Cross-trajectory counterfactual training: for each state, action sequences sampled from other trajectories serve as counterfactuals. The compatibility label is -log(Euclidean distance to the GT action + eps), trained with MSE (an InfoNCE variant was tested and dropped).
Goal-prompted variant (LWM-B-P): the goal image is fed to the observation encoder E_o(o_t, o_g) so the prediction is goal-conditioned from the start.

Pseudo-label policy learning: 64 k-means action-sequence centers are scored by LWM for random (o_t, o_g) pairs from unlabeled video, and the best one labels an autoregressive discrete-token policy trained with cross-entropy.

Imagination RL: the policy samples M_gen action sequences, LWM's discriminator gives rewards, group-normalized advantages feed a GRPO objective with KL to a reference policy, with no environment interaction.

setting.backbone: LWM world model (DINOv2-small or CroCo-v2-base encoder + causal Transformer decoders, trained end-to-end) + autoregressive Transformer action-token policy (CroCo-v2-base encoder)
setting.training_data: RECON and SCAND (about 3 h of wheeled robot data) plus a self-collected LWM dataset (about 6 h, campus/residential/park). 95/5 train/test split; half of train for world model + imitation, half for RL. Policy labels come from the world model, with no action annotations.
setting.observation: monocular RGB current image + goal image
setting.action_space: action sequences of (x,y,theta) waypoints (K up to 64, keyframe every 0.2 m), discretized into 64 k-means tokens for the policy
setting.simulator: real world only (offline datasets + real robot)
setting.privileged: none (goal image given; odometry from wheel encoders/IMU used only for dataset labels)

numbers.backbone: CroCo-v2-base policy trained via LWM pseudo-labels + GRPO
numbers.extra: six real-world scenarios; success within 0.5 m; no action annotations
goal prompt given in advance; 64 clustered candidate sequences

numbers_note: Policy-learning results (Table 2, PE/OE) and the GRPO improvement (Fig. 3) are also reported, but only Table 1 and Table 3 numbers are listed above. The real-world evaluation is small (six scenarios).
results: LWM-B-P achieves the lowest prediction error and highest action-selection accuracy on RECON, SCAND and LWM (e.g. LWM ACC3 90.6 vs 55.4 for DINO-WM and 42.43 for NWM). Policies trained from LWM pseudo-labels beat those supervised by NWM or DINO-WM, and GRPO inside LWM improves all initializations. In the real world it reaches SR 66.7 vs 33.3 for NoMaD and BC.
limitations: Relies on the assumption that spatial proximity correlates with visual similarity, which breaks under occlusion and clutter.
Real-world evaluation is small (six scenarios) and the strongest variant needs the goal supplied in advance; results are for goal-image navigation only.
The initial policy is limited to a fixed set of 64 clustered action sequences, and RL reward quality is bounded by the world model.
